definitions.explanation: The biological order Rodentia, comprising mammals such as mice, rats, squirrels, beavers, and porcupines that share continuously growing front incisors used for gnawing. Used both as a technical zoological term and in everyday writing about animals.

examples.japanese: ⟦{鼠|ねずみ}→鼠：02238_nezumi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{齧歯類|げっしるい}だ。
リスや⟦{兎|うさぎ}→兎：01854_usagi⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧{齧歯類|げっしるい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{含|ふく}まれる→含む：01982_fukumu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{思|おも}われ→思う：00492_omou⟧がちだ。
examples.english: Squirrels and rabbits are often mistakenly thought to be included among rodents.

examples.japanese: {齧歯類|げっしるい}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{哺乳類|ほにゅうるい}→哺乳類：04920_honyuurui⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{中|なか}→中：00654_naka⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{最|もっと}も→最も：01736_mottomo⟧⟦{種類|しゅるい}→種類：01560_shurui⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: Rodents are the most species-rich group within mammals.

examples.japanese: {齧歯類|げっしるい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{前歯|まえば}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{一生|いっしょう}→一生：01728_isshou⟧⟦{伸|の}び→伸びる：01974_nobiru⟧⟦{続|つづ}ける→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧⟦ため→ため：01145_tame⟧、⟦{常|つね}→常：28958_tsune⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{何|なに}か→何か：03873_nanika⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{齧|かじ}って→齧る：05126_kajiru⟧⟦{削|けず}ら→削る：03922_kezuru⟧⟦なければならない→なければならない：27600_nakerebanaranai⟧。
examples.english: Because rodents' incisors grow continuously throughout their lives, they must constantly gnaw on something to wear them down.

notes:
Composed of {齧|げっ} (to gnaw), {歯|し} (tooth), and the suffix ⟦{類|るい}→類：15121_rui⟧ (kind; class; -idae). Literally 'the gnawing-tooth class,' the name highlights the defining trait of the order — a single pair of continuously growing incisors in each jaw.

USAGE:
A biological category term, used in science writing, nature documentaries, veterinary contexts, and pet-shop literature. Like other {〜類|るい} group names (⟦{哺乳類|ほにゅうるい}→哺乳類：04920_honyuurui⟧ mammals, ⟦{爬虫類|はちゅうるい}→爬虫類：04921_hachuurui⟧ reptiles), it sounds technical but is fully comprehensible to general readers. Note that rabbits (⟦{兎|うさぎ}→兎：01854_usagi⟧) are NOT rodents — they belong to the order Lagomorpha ({兎形目|うさぎがたもく} or ウサギ{目|もく}) — though many laypeople assume otherwise.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {齧歯類|げっしるい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{属|ぞく}する→属する：12402_zokusuru⟧: to belong to the rodents
- {齧歯類|げっしるい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{動物|どうぶつ}→動物：01480_doubutsu⟧: rodent animals
- ⟦{小型|こがた}→小型：12460_kogata⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{齧歯類|げっしるい}: small rodents
- {齧歯|げっし}{目|もく}: order Rodentia (formal taxonomic term)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{哺乳類|ほにゅうるい}→哺乳類：04920_honyuurui⟧: mammals — the broader class to which rodents belong
- ⟦{鼠|ねずみ}→鼠：02238_nezumi⟧: mouse; rat — the most familiar example of a rodent
- {兎形目|うさぎがたもく}: order Lagomorpha — the order containing rabbits and hares (often confused with rodents)
- ⟦{爬虫類|はちゅうるい}→爬虫類：04921_hachuurui⟧: reptiles — a parallel taxonomic group of similar formality
